items.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001
items.q: like a Mozart his mind worked

ctx.x: At the piano? To see if—

Yes. To see if I’m close to right. And I know that my teacher Darius Milhaud never had to check anything and never had to be near a piano, and like a Mozart his mind worked, just some kind of perfection that God gave a few people. Stravinsky always wrote at the piano.
That’s interesting. The ideas that you’ve had in jazz, the polytonality and polyrhythmic, do you try to get those into your orchestral pieces also?

items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was trying to be amusing by using Mozart’s term.

ctx.x: On that Turkey date, I think it’s important to mention a group, Blue Rondo a la Turk.

I was on my way to a radio station to be interviewed in Turkey. I was walking through the streets. There were street musicians playing in 9/8. [Brubeck sings a 9/8 rhythmic pattern.] Like that. So when I got to the radio station, there was a wonderful musician named June [ ], a friend of Gunther Schuller. I said to June, “What is this rhythm? di-ya di-ya di-ya ta-ta-ta di-ya di-ya.” He turned and looked at the band and pointed, and the whole band started playing something in 9/8 with that rhythm.
